item.title: SEA’s digital consumer credit loan book reaches estimated $19.8 billion at the end of first half
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Southeast Asia’s digital consumer credit loan book reached an estimated $19.8 billion at the end of the first half of 2026, according to Momentum Works’ latest report.
item.content:encoded:
Southeast Asia’s digital consumer credit loan book reached an estimated $19.8 billion at the end of the first half of 2026, according to Momentum Works’ latest report.

The Consumer Credit in Southeast Asia 2026 report showed on Monday that Indonesia leads the region with $8.6 billion in outstanding loans, followed by the Philippines at $4.3 billion and Thailand at US$2.9 billion.

Sea Group’s Monee alone makes up about 45 percent of the total loan book, making it the largest lender in the region.

Monee’s reported loan book reached $12.6 billion in the third quarter of 2026 (including Brazil and SME lending), nearly quadrupling since the first quarter of 2024.

Personal cash loans and off-Shopee Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) now account for about 60 percent of Monee’s total loan book, while its standalone apps are among the top of the Finance category app rankings in their respective markets.

The top four players, Monee, Grab, GoTo and GCash, account for about 60 percent.

Meanwhile, the report highlighted that TikTok Shop will almost certainly scale its own consumer credit business in Southeast Asia.

It noted that TikTok Shop brings a sizeable commerce operation, transaction data and access to ByteDance’s experience developing consumer credit through Douyin in China.

Its lending arm PIPO (Payments In, Payments Out) is already offering financing in Thailand, the Philippines and Malaysia, using different local arrangements.

Momentum Works believes its new standalone shopping app gives TikTok Shop greater freedom to integrate and promote credit, supporting both purchase conversion and lending growth.

Grab’s proposed acquisition of Atome Financial, on the other hand, shows the value of combining lending expertise with platform distribution.

As platforms bring credit in-house, Momentum Works said independent BNPL providers face growing pressure. Market consolidation puts greater pressure on independent BNPL providers than on established cash lenders.

The report also showed that large platforms and wallets are best placed to capture the next wave of credit growth.

Momentum Works sees substantial room for growth in the region’s US$19.8 billion digital consumer credit market, with large players likely to capture much of the upside, provided execution remains disciplined and regulation stable.

The window for new independent players to achieve scale and venture-level exits has closed, it added.

item.title: MetaComp scales interoperable payment network to advance cross-border payments in ASEAN
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: MetaComp Pte. Ltd., a Singapore-headquartered Web2.5 payments solutions provider, is expanding its StableX Agentic Network to facilitate more cross-border payments into and across Southeast Asia, targeting banks, payment service providers and businesses.
item.content:encoded:
MetaComp Pte. Ltd., a Singapore-headquartered Web2.5 payments solutions provider, is expanding its StableX Agentic Network to facilitate more cross-border payments into and across Southeast Asia, targeting banks, payment service providers and businesses.

The network, which connects payment systems across currencies and markets, has grown to more than 1,000 members and over 100,000 users in its first year, the company said in a statement on Wednesday.

The expansion comes as Southeast Asia’s digital economy continues to grow. Google, Temasek and Bain & Company project the region’s digital economy will reach US$368 billion in gross merchandise value (GMV) this year, up 17 percent from 2025.

Meanwhile, merchandise trade among ASEAN member states reached US$2.1 trillion in the first half of 2025, a 16.4 percent year-on-year increase, according to the ASEAN Secretariat.

Despite the growth, businesses making cross-border payments in the region continue to navigate fragmented payment systems, currencies and regulatory requirements across individual markets. Networks connecting these systems could help facilitate trade by making payments more accessible across borders.

The StableX Agentic Network is designed to connect traditional fiat payment rails with stable coin networks, routing transactions through available channels based on exchange rates and payment conditions. Its members include payment service providers serving clients seeking to expand into Southeast Asia, including exporters from North Asia.

The network also provides alternative settlement routes when a particular payment corridor is slow or unavailable. In April, MetaComp announced that it would adopt Solana as a preferred blockchain for settlement, adding another route alongside traditional fiat payment channels.

Through local payment rails and the SWIFT network, participating institutions can make payments in local currencies across six ASEAN markets: Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam, the Philippines and Thailand. They can also collect local-currency payments in Singapore, the Philippines and Indonesia, with Vietnam expected to be added later.

A key feature of the network is its support for payments initiated by both humans and artificial intelligence (AI) agents, with governance controls built into the system.

MetaComp’s StableX Know Your Agent (KYA) Framework serves as a verification and governance mechanism for AI agents operating on the network. Each agent must be registered to a verified owner, operate within assigned permissions and remain traceable to the party responsible for it.

Launched in April 2026, the framework has since been productized and deployed. It monitors agents throughout their lifecycle, using more than 30 measures across six governance objectives to assess their behavior. The results are displayed on a live dashboard.

Transactions are also screened through VisionX, MetaComp’s compliance intelligence engine, which monitors activity across both fiat and blockchain-based payment channels.

Separately, VisionX AI, a standalone regulatory technology company within Alpha Ladder Group, unveiled AEGIS, its proprietary Large Graph Model for financial crime detection, and launched TraceX, a blockchain investigation platform at the forum.

Tin Pei Ling, Co-President of MetaComp, said the region’s ambition for integrated payments would require infrastructure capable of facilitating transactions across markets.

“ASEAN has set a clear ambition for integrated payments, and policy only becomes trade when payments can move between markets,” she said.

She added that the StableX KYA framework was designed to ensure AI agents operating on the network were verified, operated within defined boundaries and remained accountable.

Bo Bai, Executive Chairman and Co-founder of Alpha Ladder Group, MetaComp’s parent company, said Southeast Asia was an increasingly important growth market for the group’s clients.

He said the company intended to extend the network into more regional markets, supported by new investment, while connecting businesses from North Asia and elsewhere to Southeast Asia.

item.title: Taiwan’s Delta Electronics to raises Malaysian unit’s capital by $120M
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Taiwan-headquartered Delta Electronics, a provider of power, thermal, and automation solutions, has increased its investment in its wholly-owned Malaysian unit by MYR490.92 million ($120 million), to expand production sites.
item.content:encoded:
Taiwan-headquartered Delta Electronics, a provider of power, thermal, and automation solutions, has increased its investment in its wholly-owned Malaysian unit by MYR490.92 million ($120 million), to expand production sites.

In a filing with the Taiwan Stock Exchange (TWSE) dated November 16, Delta Electronics said Delta Electronics International (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. will subscribe for 490.9 million common shares of Delta Electronics International (Malaysia) Sdn. Bhd. at MYR1 each. The transaction took place on the same day.

After the investment, Delta Electronic’ cumulative holding in the Malaysian unit will reach 612.3 million shares ($150 million).

Delta Electronics, serving data centers, energy infrastructure, telecom infrastructure, reported consolidated sales revenue for October 2026 of TWD74,666 million ($2.27 billion), up 30.1 percent year-on-year. By business category, power electronics accounted for 51 percent of October sales, infrastructure for 36 percent, automation for 8 percent, and mobility for 5 percent.

Its cumulative consolidated revenue for January-October 2026 reached TWD614,334 million ($18.69 billion), up 36.3 percent year-on-year.

item.title: Singapore sets out PayNow Generation 2 Implementation Roadmap
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) has on Wednesday published an implementation roadmap to accelerate the next phase of PayNow’s development.
item.content:encoded:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) has on Wednesday published an implementation roadmap to accelerate the next phase of PayNow’s development.

The roadmap will close the critical gaps identified in Phase 1 of PayNow Generation 2, the duo said in a statement.

The upcoming enhancements will make payments simpler, safer and more accessible, expanding the range of payments that PayNow can support and enabling programmable payment processes for businesses and government agencies. These are set out in the Phase 2 report for PayNow Generation 2 (PayNow Gen2).

The PayNow Gen2 implementation roadmap was developed following extensive consultations with end users, including e-commerce users, small merchants, Singapore residents and inbound tourists.

Industry workshops were also conducted with banks, payment service providers, payment technology firms, marketplaces and government agencies to co-design and validate proposed enhancements and work through practical implementation considerations.

Over 2027 and 2028, MAS will lead the Singapore Payments Network (SPaN), Banking Computer Services (BCS) and industry and public sector partners to drive timely delivery of the following PayNow Gen2 enhancements.

These included QR interoperability via SGQR+. With SGQR+, Singaporeans will be able to use their preferred payment app to make payments at any merchant, without needing to check which QR schemes are accepted by the merchant.

Tourists will similarly be able to benefit from this QR interoperability. In addition, as Singapore connects to more major regional QR networks through SGQR+, this will enable more merchants in Singapore to receive tourist payments from a wider pool of foreign payment networks, and Singaporeans to pay through local apps in more countries.

Work on the SGQR+ switch has begun, with a limited rollout in 2027 and expanding in scope in 2028.

Other enhancements included deep-linking, with online payments via PayNow will be faster and simpler. Users will be able to progress seamlessly from an e-commerce site to their preferred payment application without saving and retrieving payment QR code screenshots from their phone gallery to complete a payment.

Today, deep linking by some financial institutions in selected e-commerce checkouts and government agencies is already live, and MAS wants to make this more widely adopted.

By end-2027, the development of common technical standards and a central facility for deep-linking will support more consistent, safe, and seamless e-commerce payment journeys as these linkages are added progressively over 2028.

The enhancements also involved higher-value payments. With higher PayNow limits, Singaporeans will be able to make and receive higher-value government payments with immediate confirmation, starting with a limited rollout with one government agency in late 2027, followed by a targeted rollout to other government agencies from 2028.

They also included PayNow person-to-merchant (P2M) rules and dispute resolution. SPaN will develop clearer and more consistent rules for payment disputes, refunds, fraud and scams that may arise from PayNow transactions.

Such safeguards will be introduced in stages over 2028, with SPaN providing scheme governance and oversight.

Data fields is also one of the enhancements. It is noted that enhanced PayNow data fields carrying richer, structured payment information3 will help businesses and government agencies automate payment processing and reconciliation to improve payment efficiency.

Enhanced data fields are targeted to be introduced from end-2027. This will enable services
using this data to start being offered in 2028 onwards.

MAS said it will convene SPaN, BCS and other key partners to innovate new capabilities for emerging types of payments, including those made through AI agents.

ABS, banks, payment service providers and other industry participants will also carry out solution validation testing for economically processing very small, high-frequency payments and high-volume payments.

Work on smarter business payments will examine tokenized payment credentials for recurring and contactless payments, while richer payment information will lay the groundwork for greater automation and for AI-driven and programmable payments, said the statement.

Separately, MAS said it will also develop the Future Payment Rails Blueprint in 2027.

Building on PayNow Gen2, the Blueprint will set out a design for Singapore’s payment infrastructure to serve an increasingly digital, connected and automated economy.

It will define a multi-rail, multi-functional and multi-service payments architecture, guided by four objectives: lower operating costs, faster time-to-market for new products and features, greater resilience of the national payment rails and timely innovation.

item.title: CEVA Logistics, SIT launch innovation lab to bring flexible automation to warehouses
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: CEVA Logistics, a global third-party logistics firm, and the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT), Singapore’s University for Industry, have jointly launched the Intelligent Logistics & Autonomous Systems (ILAS) Lab on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
CEVA Logistics, a global third-party logistics firm, and the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT), Singapore’s University for Industry, have jointly launched the Intelligent Logistics & Autonomous Systems (ILAS) Lab on Tuesday.

As logistics operations face workforce constraints and growing pressure to improve productivity, the ILAS Lab will develop automation aimed at executing repetitive, labor-intensive tasks, freeing warehouse teams to focus on more specialized, skilled tasks, CEVA Logistics said in a statement.

The five-year collaboration will build on CEVA’s strengths by developing adaptable automation in high-mix, low-volume value-added services (VAS) operations.

The work will combine CEVA’s logistics expertise with SIT’s expertise in robotics, artificial intelligence (AI) vision systems and connected automation to develop and validate solutions for kitting, labeling and packing varied products in small batches.

It is noted that value-added services represent a major share of activity across CEVA’s global operations.

At the Blue Hub facility—the company’s automated, multi-sector facility in Singapore—VAS alone accounts for approximately half of all warehouse floor hours.

CEVA aims to advance its existing VAS capabilities through the ILAS Lab’s intelligent automation technologies to create adaptable assembly lines that can accommodate rapidly shifting, market-driven customer requirements.

Solutions developed through ILAS projects are expected to be deployed at CEVA’s Blue Hub facility within the next one two years, demonstrating how applied research can be translated into real-world logistics applications.

The research will also explore AI-enabled vision and sensing, as well as connected automation that brings robotics, software and operational systems together.

Solutions will be tested and validated under relevant operational conditions. Suitable applications will then progress to pilots and field trials to assess their technical performance, operational suitability and potential for deployment at CEVA’s operations.

The collaboration will build technical capabilities through joint research and knowledge exchange, while supporting talent development for the logistics sector.

Since 2023, more than 130 SIT students and graduates have gained exposure to CEVA’s operations. SIT students will have opportunities to contribute to applied research and innovation activities undertaken at ILAS.

Supported by the Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) and National Robotics Program (NRP), the joint lab will develop, validate and deploy logistics automation solutions to advance Singapore’s logistics capabilities and competitiveness.

“The joint innovation lab is part of CEVA’s vision for the Warehouse of Tomorrow. Working with SIT, we aim to bring adaptable automation from applied research into everyday operations, helping our teams improve efficiency and respond to changing customer requirements,

“Our ambition is to build on validated solutions for new applications across customer sectors and our Asia Pacific network, using lessons from each deployment to shape further innovation,” said Guy Meredith, Contract Logistics Vice President, APAC CEVA Logistics.

Susanna Leong, Deputy President (Academic) & Provost Singapore Institute of Technology, said impactful innovation happens when research is applied to real industry challenges.

“The ILAS Lab brings our students and researchers into the heart of logistics operations, where they can work alongside CEVA to develop and validate robotics and AI solutions for real-world needs,

“This allows us to advance innovation while developing talent with the skills and experience to contribute to the transformation of the logistics sector,” she added.

Junie Fo， Vice President and Head, Logistics and Supply Chain Management，EDB，said the ILAS Lab demonstrates how industry-academia collaboration can accelerate innovation and transformation in Singapore’s logistics sector.

“By bringing together CEVA Logistics’ operational expertise and SIT’s applied research capabilities, this partnership is well-positioned to develop intelligent automation solutions that address real industry challenges,” she added.

item.title: Vietnam proposes 99% purity standard for rare earth exports
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Vietnam seeks to allow exports of rare earth products only if they are deeply processed, with most individual oxides and metals required to reach at least 99 percent total rare earth content.
item.content:encoded:
Vietnam seeks to allow exports of rare earth products only if they are deeply processed, with most individual oxides and metals required to reach at least 99 percent total rare earth content.

The standards are set out in Annex III of a draft circular on mineral exports, compiled by the Ministry of Industry and Trade. The draft document has yet to set an implementation date.

For separated oxides, the draft requires total rare earth oxide content of at least 99 percent for nearly every product, with cerium oxide lower at 98 percent.

The share of the oxide inside that total must also meet its own threshold. It is 99 percent for lanthanum, praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, dysprosium, and erbium oxides, and 99.5 percent for gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and ytterbium oxides.

Thulium, lutetium and yttrium oxides must reach 99.9 percent. Europium oxide is the strictest at 99.99 percent. Scandium oxide must be at least 99.9 percent by mass.

Individual rare earth metals face a similar requirement. Total metal content must be at least 99 percent, or 99.5 percent for praseodymium. The target metal’s share must be 99 to 99.9 percent depending on the element.

The annex also sets standards for alloys, alloy powders and permanent magnets. A neodymium-iron-boron alloy must contain at least 28 percent rare earth metal and 0.8 to 1.5 percent boron. A sintered neodymium-iron-boron magnet must have remanence of at least 1.08 tesla, intrinsic coercivity of at least 955 kilo-amperes per metre and a maximum energy product of at least 223 kilojoules per cubic metre.

Beyond the standard, a rare earth product can be exported only if it is also on the Prime Minister’s list of deeply processed products.

Vietnam’s rare earth resources are estimated in the ministry’s report at about 19.82 million tons of rare earth oxide, mainly in Lai Chau and Lao Cai provinces in the north.

item.title: Malaysia unveils Sukuk financing scheme to mobilize global capital for climate adaptation and resilience
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: The Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) has on Wednesday introduced the Sukuk PRISMA to the global market, a new purpose-driven sustainable sukuk framework designed to mobilize capital for climate adaptation and resilience, supporting wider sustainable development priorities.
item.content:encoded:
The Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) has on Wednesday introduced the Sukuk PRISMA to the global market, a new purpose-driven sustainable sukuk framework designed to mobilize capital for climate adaptation and resilience, supporting wider sustainable development priorities.

The framework aligns Malaysia’s national priorities with the ASEAN Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance, the International Capital Market Association (ICMA) Principles1, the UN Sustainable Development Goals and internationally accepted Shariah standards, SC said in a statement.

Sukuk PRISMA represents the next strategic evolution of Malaysia’s landmark Sustainable and Responsible Investment (SRI) Sukuk framework introduced in 2014.

Building on Malaysia’s global leadership in Islamic capital markets, Sukuk PRISMA expands the capital market’s scope beyond conventional green and social categories to encompass broader climate adaptation, resilience and transitional financing. This includes flood mitigation, coastal protection, agriculture and the resilience of power grids.

It also supports sukuk issuances denominated in ringgit and major hard currencies, enabling access to international capital and connecting global investors with high-impact sustainable investment opportunities.

“The framework introduces a broader and clearer thematic classification to support national sustainability agenda, making it more investable, enhances investor understanding and strengthens Malaysia’s position as a leader in sustainable and Islamic finance,” SC Chairman Mohammad Faiz Azmi said.

According to the statement, Sukuk PRISMA also advances the aspirations of the Capital Market Masterplan 2026-2030 (CMP) by facilitating greater private capital mobilization towards sustainable development priorities while strengthening Malaysia’s leadership in sustainable and Islamic finance.

The SC will issue the Sukuk PRISMA Framework in the first quarter of 2027. Ahead of its issuance, the SC will undertake engagements with issuers, investors and other market participants to support market readiness and encourage early adoption.

Arthur Joseph Kurup, Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability launched the Sukuk PRISMA at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye.

In conjunction with the launch, the SC exchanged memoranda of understanding (MOUs) with three partners to strengthen Malaysia’s sustainability ecosystem and deepen capital market development.

The first MOU with the Malaysian Green Technology and Climate Change Corporation (MGTC) aims to formalize cooperation on sustainability matters, including adaptation and resilience financing, carbon markets and sustainability reporting.

The second MOU with Credit Guarantee and Investment Facility (CGIF) aims to deepen Malaysia’s ringgit bond and sukuk market, including through the promotion of Sukuk PRISMA and the facilitation of pilot issuances. CGIF is a trust fund of the Asian Development Bank.

The third MOU with University of Durham: Aims to deepen collaboration in research, capacity building and thought leadership in Islamic and sustainable finance, and climate litigation, among others.

item.title: 94 percent of Singapore small business owners surveyed say more AI guidance is needed
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: 94 percent of Singapore small business owners surveyed agree that small businesses need more guidance to gain the full benefits of artificial intelligence (AI), according to YouGov research commissioned by Meta revealed on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
94 percent of Singapore small business owners surveyed agree that small businesses need more guidance to gain the full benefits of artificial intelligence (AI), according to YouGov research commissioned by Meta revealed on Tuesday.

The research also found that 82 percent of Singapore small business owners surveyed whose business has used AI report a positive impact on productivity over the past 12 months.

Among Singapore small business owners who report a positive impact on productivity, 62 percent use time saved through AI to improve the quality of existing work.

Meanwhile, customer engagement is one area where owners see opportunities for AI. In Singapore, 52 percent of small business owners surveyed have used or would be interested in using AI-powered customer responses.

The research was commissioned by Meta and conducted online by YouGov among 3,983 small business owners across Australia, Singapore, Vietnam, Indonesia, Taiwan, India, Thailand, Japan and Hong Kong. Data was collected between August 6 and September 2, 2026.

Within each market, quotas were applied by business size to achieve a broad and balanced spread across businesses with 1–9, 10–19 and 20–49 employees.

The findings provide insights across a diverse cross-section of small businesses in each market, rather than being nationally representative of the small business population.

Reported adoption and impact differ across the nine markets surveyed. These differences may partly reflect how owners in each market interpret the questions, as well as translation and local survey response norms.

item.title: Weixin Pay, Grab report several-fold growth in Singapore
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Weixin Pay and Grab said the transaction value and volume of their payments partnership have grown several times over since launch, as they marked its first anniversary in Singapore.
item.content:encoded:
Weixin Pay and Grab said the transaction value and volume of their payments partnership have grown several times over since launch, as they marked its first anniversary in Singapore.

In a statement on Wednesday, Weixin Pay said the service lets Chinese visitors pay with Weixin Pay in the Grab app and at local merchants in Singapore.

The two companies first worked together in 2022 through a Grab mini program inside Weixin, the Chinese app known outside China as WeChat. They signed a memorandum of understanding in 2025 to expand into in-app payments and QR interoperability. The service went live in May 2026.

Weixin Pay is now an in-app payment option in the Grab app in Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Cambodia. In Singapore, Weixin Pay also works with Grab QR codes at local merchants. Visitors can use it for Grab rides, food deliveries, and GrabMart orders, or scan Grab QR codes at restaurants, hawker centers, and shops.

The companies said total payment volume, transaction value, and active users have all grown several times over in Singapore since launch, with growth each month and October the highest month to date for all three.

Kanika Maheshwari, head of Grab Financial Group in Singapore, said the partnership had exceeded expectations. Chinese travelers trust the familiar Grab app when buying from local merchants. The merchants in popular food and tourist areas are seeing higher sales, the executive added. She cited a hawker’s comment that a customer paid in RMB and he received SGD instantly.

Gary Wong, head of innovative and strategic partnerships at Weixin Pay Southeast Asia, said Chinese visitors can pay for a ride or a meal without working out another payment method or exchanging currency. “Together with our partners, we want to bring this convenience to more places,” he said.

The companies plan to add features that let travelers find local recommendations and claim vouchers before arriving. They also aim to bring the payment service to other Southeast Asian markets.

item.title: Singapore launches initiatives to support National AI Missions for financial services
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Future of Finance Institute (FFI) have on Wednesday jointly announced initiatives in support of the National AI Missions for financial services.
item.content:encoded:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Future of Finance Institute (FFI) have on Wednesday jointly announced initiatives in support of the National AI Missions for financial services.

The National AI Missions for financial services aim to strengthen financial crime prevention, improve access to financing for businesses and enable artificial intelligence (AI) agents to transact safely, the duo said in a joint statement.

MAS and FFI will support the implementation of these missions through initiatives that provide data for AI development and testing, enable safe experimentation with agentic transactions and strengthen the AI capabilities and talent needed across the financial sector.

FFI will work with MAS under the AI Innovation Arena initiative to provide developers and solution providers with relevant synthetic data to build and test AI solutions that advance the AI Missions for financial services, and other potential real-world industry challenges.

The Innovation Arena will initially support the mission to strengthen financial crime prevention with MAS providing access to a synthetic dataset that can be used to develop and test AI solutions for scam detection.

Technology firms, AI labs, solution providers and research institutions are welcome to submit an express of interest for access to the cross-institution synthetic dataset via this form.

Over time, the Innovation Arena could support other AI Missions with relevant industry challenges and datasets.

FFI will establish an Agentic Money Sandbox, which provides a controlled environment for financial institutions to develop and test how AI agents can transact using digital money within defined authority, limits and safeguards.

Initial use cases will include agent-initiated payments and treasury management across participating financial institutions.

The Sandbox will enable participants to test the controls and arrangements needed for AI agents to transact safely before such use cases are deployed in live environments.

FFI will also work with A*STAR’s Institute of Advanced Intelligence and Computing (IAIC) to
advance the locally grounded speech-to-text AI work, previously announced by MAS, into live pilots for practical financial-sector applications.

One application being explored is the use of speech-to-text capabilities to support real-time compliance monitoring for operational risk management.

The collaboration with A*STAR IAIC will also explore other AI capabilities for financial services, including generative AI guardrails.

FFI will additionally partner AI Singapore (AISG) to build AI talent for the financial sector such as through apprentice programs, drawing on AISG’s AI expertise and connections beyond the financial sector.

MAS and FFI also unveiled FFI’s financial institutions launch partners — DBS, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB, together with FFI’s technology and research partners, will bring complementary expertise and capabilities to address shared industry needs and develop practical applications in support of the National AI Missions for financial services and FFI’s broader program of work.

These initiatives were set out by Gan Kim Yong, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Energy, Trade and Industry (Trade), and Chairman of MAS at the Singapore FinTech Festival on Wednesday.
